pairs.subject_desc_a: C1 47.40% is a footprint claim scored as capability
pairs.pair_note: seeded draw from the cross-seat candidate universe
pairs.state_finding_a:
FINDING (seat: dsv41f)
severity: major
artifact: C1 (E-Q13, chain tip d852e6ac...)
finding: C1's headline 47.40% bytes-gain is a footprint/encoding claim, not a capability claim, yet it is scored on the twin-delivery task where C2 already shows the wormhole is the load-bearing mechanism. The two arms differ in encoding (1-byte intra-cell vs 2-byte tauPlane/dPlane) AND in whether the tau plane is SRAM-resident (the receipted cached-port caveat). So the 47.40% conflates encoding density with cache residency; the 'ticks identical' line is the only control that partially separates them, and it does not price the SRAM cost. The founder's 25% guess being beaten is presented as vindication, but a 2x footprint reduction mechanically caps bytes-gain near 50% -- 47.40% is close to the encoding ceiling, not a surprising result.
pairs.state_finding_b:
FINDING (seat: nemotron35sv)
severity: major
artifact: M4 wormhole table (64-slot, content-addressed, last-writer-wins) and E-Q14 provenance autopsy
finding: The wormhole table is content-addressed on a 6-bit d (64 slots) with last-writer-wins collisions, so distinct Abstain cells sharing d clobber each other's resonance by construction. E-Q14 confirms this bites even in the nominal zero-pollution arm: an adjacent-d convoy compresses provenance and the slot-63 saturation rail becomes a "party line," with the zero-pollution arm itself failing its floor at pollution fraction 0.94. The "80/80 robust to polluters" result measures delivery, not provenance correctness, so twin-resonance provenance is fragile by design, not merely under load.
